title: Fuzz harness for function-call schema drift and streaming edge-case regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We've observed intermittent failures across SDKs and model variants where function-call payloads and structured outputs drift slightly from the contract (extra keys, truncated arrays, out-of-order streaming chunks). These surface as client parse errors or subtle semantic regressions. Goal: implement a deterministic fuzzing harness that synthesizes realistic malformed and near-valid function-call outputs plus streaming chunk anomalies, run it across model variants and SDK adapters, and gate CI on the absence of new unique failures.

Scope: the harness should cover: (1) schema drift in function-call arguments (extra/missing fields, type coercions, nested array truncation), (2) streaming-level anomalies (split JSON across chunks, reordering, duplicate chunks, truncated final token), and (3) interactions with KV-cache prefixing that change timing and chunk boundaries. The harness will produce minimal reproducer payloads, failure fingerprints, and suggested guardrails (parsers robustness tests / SDK-level parsing changes).
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic harness that can produce >= 500 synthetic variants for a given prompt template
CI job that runs the harness against two model variants (open-1.3, redwood-slim-1) and the JS/Python SDK adapters with single-run timeout <= 20m
All newly discovered failures get recorded as tickets or appended to existing flaky-tests list with repro payload and fingerprint
Documented mitigation patterns (SDK parsing retry/backoff, streaming reassembly heuristics) included in the test output
No regression introduced in existing structured-output contract tests when running the harness in nightly mode
test_plan: Phase 1: Local dev harness — seed corpus from existing golden/canonical prompts plus mutated real customer examples (10k seeds)
Phase 2: CI integration — add a lightweight smoke run to PR checks (100 variants) and a nightly full run (1k variants)
Phase 3: Cross-model sweep — run nightly across model variants and record differences per-model in the conformance dashboard
Phase 4: Triage automations — auto-create tickets for novel fingerprints and attach minimal reproducer to the ticket
steps: Design mutation strategies for function-call shapes and streaming chunk boundaries
Implement harness runner with deterministic rng seed, pluggable model adapters, and SDK wrappers
Integrate with existing conformance infra (fingerprinter service + flaky-test registry)
Add lightweight PR job and a scheduled nightly job in CI
Run initial sweep, triage results, and create follow-ups for SDK fixes or runtime hardening
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes attached; primary design decision is to keep mutations model-agnostic and let the fingerprinter cluster by semantic signature rather than raw bytes.
2026-02-25 - Diego Ramos: PoC harness implemented locally. Found 7 unique failure fingerprints against the JS SDK caused by streaming chunk reassembly. Filed ENG-19932 for JS SDK parser hardening.
2026-03-01 - Clara Nguyen (PM): Prioritize adding the PR smoke check to avoid regressions; keep nightly full-run but make result triage async to reduce CI noise.
2026-03-04 - Security review: quick pass — no secrets are stored; harness runs with limited test keys. No full security review required at this stage.

2026-03-05 - Diego Ramos: Integrated the harness into the conformance runner and added the PR job. First CI smoke run flagged a flaky failure (fingerprint F-0b9) linked to model redwood-slim-1 stream truncation. Creating follow-up with runtime team.
notes: Implementation should avoid overfitting to existing golden prompts — generation logic must include stochastic but reproducible mutations
Keep the harness independent of production traffic; use recorded anonymized examples and synthesized variants
Aim for clear triage signals: include model hash, SDK version, rng seed, and exact chunk offsets in any failure report
